nodes.name: Iron sheet pretreatment
nodes.procedure: Iron sheets of 1 cm×2 cm were used as the substrate of electrodeposition. The rust on the surface of the iron substrates were cleaned by 1000# sandpaper, and then the surface oxides and oil stains were removed by soaking in hydrochloric acid with a volume ratio of 1:1 and 1:3 ultrasonic for 1 min. The iron substrates were rinsed by anhydrous ethanol and ultra-pure water, and finally stored in anhydrous ethanol to prevent secondary oxidation.

nodes.name: HEA-FMCC electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The electrodeposited fluid consists of 25 gL⁻¹ CoSO₄·6H₂O, 22.6 gL⁻¹ MnSO₄·H₂O, 23.33 gL⁻¹ FeSO₄·7H₂O, 21 gL⁻¹ CuSO₄·5H₂O, 7.65 gL⁻¹ Na₃PO₄·12H₂O, 15 gL⁻¹ H₃BO₃, 70.35 gL⁻¹ Na₃C₆H₅O₇ and 10 ml 1M H₂SO₄. And slowly adjust pH to be around 6.5. The Hg/HgO electrode was used as reference electrode (RE), the catalyst samples were used as the working electrode (WE) and the platinum electrode was used as counter electrode (CE). The one-step electrodeposition was conducted using chrono potential method with a CHI920c electrochemical working station, and the deposition parameters were set as 100 mA cm⁻² and 3600s. After that, the HEA-FMCC modified Fe substrate was immersed in electrodeposition solution for 3 min to stable coating. The prepared HEA-FMCC was cleaned with ultra-pure water and anhydrous ethanol.

nodes.name: HEA-NFMCC corrosion engineering
nodes.procedure: The prepared HEA-FMCC was cleaned with ultra-pure water and anhydrous ethanol, and then catalysts were corroded for 24 h under different concentrations of NiCl₂ solutions at room temperature, including 0.25 molL⁻¹, 0.5 molL⁻¹, 0.75 molL⁻¹ and 1.00 molL⁻¹, and were named HEA-25Ni, HEA-50Ni, HEA-75Ni and HEA-100Ni, respectively. The sample was suspended in the center of the etching solution with a Teflon electrode clamp and stirred appropriately. The electrodes were slowly and carefully cleaned with deionized water to afford the HEA-NFMCC catalysts. The catalysts were dried in 50°C oven at least 1 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: HEA-FMCC shows FCC and BCC structures with diffraction peaks at 43.34°(111), 44.43°(110), 50.39°(200), 74.04°(220), 89.87°(311). HEA-50Ni shows disappearance of Cu (110) phase and increased intensity of other peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From XRD resulted shown in Fig. 1 (a), the HEA-FMCC mainly consists FCC and BCC structures, with the main diffraction peaks located at 43.34°, 44.43°, 50.39°, 74.04° and 89.87° indexed to the (111), (110), (200), (220) and (311), respectively. After the corrosion engineering treatment in 0.5 molL⁻¹ NiCl₂, the (110) phase of Cu is observed to disappear, and the diffraction intensity of other crystal planes increased in HEA-50Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: HEA-FMCC shows no significant peaks. HEA-50Ni shows peaks at 532 cm⁻¹ and 686 cm⁻¹ attributed to metal hydroxide and metal oxide.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1(b), no significant peaks are observed for HEA-FMCC (dark blue line), since the metals do not exhibit polarizability change. However, some peaks were detected on the corroded HEA samples, where the peaks at 532 and 686 cm⁻¹ were attributed to the metal hydroxide and metal oxide.

nodes.characterization_summary: HEA-FMCC shows baseline spectrum. Corroded samples show peaks at 3519, 3422, and 1000 cm⁻¹ related to hydroxide formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with the spectrum of HEA-FMCC (dark blue line), peaks at 3519, 3422, and 1000 cm⁻¹ were observed on corroded HEA-FMCC samples (Fig, 1c), which could be related to the formation of hydroxides.

nodes.characterization_summary: HEA-FMCC shows chaotic sheet self-supporting structure. HEA-50Ni shows dense cauliflower structure aggregated with nanoscale spherical particles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to Fig. 2(a-c), before corrosion approach, the surface of the HEA-FMCC is a chaotic sheet self-supporting structure... During the corrosion immersion... become conscious of a dense cauliflower structure on the surface of HEA-50Ni (Fig. 2(d-f)).

nodes.characterization_summary: HEA-50Ni shows nanosheet layers with lattice spacing of 0.2054 nm corresponding to Cu (111) plane and partial amorphous phases on surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to Fig. 2 (g), the surface structure of HEA-50Ni exhibited abundant nanosheet layers... The crystal lattice spacing of 0.2054 nm could correspond to the (111) plane of Cu.

nodes.characterization_summary: HEA-50Ni SAED patterns show rings corresponding to (111), (200) and (220) reflections.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The structural composition of HEA-50Ni was further conformed by selected region electron diffraction (SAED) patterns in Fig. 2 (i). The rings are corresponded to the (111), (200) and (220) reflections of HEA-50Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: HEA-50Ni shows even distribution of Ni, Fe, Mn, Cu, Co elements. HEA-FMCC shows uniform distribution of Fe:Mn:Co:Cu ≈ 3:2:3:2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: STEM-EDS mapping in Fig. 2 (j) reveals the distribution of different elements (Ni, Fe, Mn, Cu, Co), and all five elements are evenly distributed on the catalyst. According to Fig. S4, STEM-EDS mapping profile of HEA-FMCC... proportion of Fe: Mn:Co:Cu elements approximately being 3:2:3:2.

nodes.characterization_summary: HEA-50Ni shows Fe³⁺ (713.69, 725.79 eV), Co³⁺ (781.54, 797.47 eV), Cu⁺/Cu²⁺ (933.49, 935.79 eV), higher valence Mn (643.46 eV), Ni²⁺/Ni³⁺ (856.77, 859.23 eV) indicating formation of high-valence hydroxides/oxyhydroxides.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental compositions and valence states of catalysts were qualitatively analyzed by XPS... Hence Ni 2p was mainly nickel hydroxide for HEA-50Ni include Ni²⁺ and Ni³⁺, which prove that the diversified high valence states hydroxyl oxides were formed by oxygen corrosion.

nodes.characterization_summary: HEA-50Ni after 100h OER at 50 mA cm⁻² shows subtle peak at ~35° ascribed to new Co-Fe precipitation phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown the XRD patterns in Fig. S7... the HEA-50Ni exhibited a subtle peak at approximately 35°, which can be ascribed to the formation of a new Co-Fe precipitation phase resulting from extended stability testing of the sample under OER conditions.

nodes.characterization_summary: HEA-50Ni after 100h OER maintains intact cauliflower morphology with nanosheet structures, showing good structural stability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: However, according to Fig. 5 (e-h), the HEA-50Ni exhibited good stability with the surface morphology of the sample remaining almost unchanged, and a mass of nanosheet structures was observed on the catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: HEA-50Ni after 100h OER shows Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺, Co²⁺/Co³⁺, Cu²⁺, Mn²⁺/Mn³⁺/Mn⁴⁺, Ni²⁺/Ni³⁺ with partial hydroxide-to-oxide conversion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the above tests, it is shown that there is a small partial conversion of hydroxides to oxides after 100 h OER operation at 50 mA cm⁻², and excellent stability is also proved.
